folds.text: A **hook** is a shell command that Claude Code runs automatically at a set moment, like after a file edit. Certain actions then always happen, instead of relying on Claude to remember.
Hooks attach to events. For example, one event fires before a tool runs and can block it. Another fires after a tool succeeds. Another fires when Claude needs your input.
Handy uses: tidy code after every edit, get a desktop notification when Claude is waiting for you, or stop edits to protected files before they happen.
You add hooks in a settings file. Type `/hooks` in a session to browse the ones you have. Hooks run commands on your machine, so only add ones you understand.
Hooks and **CLAUDE.md** differ. CLAUDE.md is guidance Claude may or may not follow. A hook is enforced by the program itself, so use one for rules that cannot have exceptions.
